# Lab Report With Working Shown

A fixed report skeleton, repeated across fourteen deliverables, in which **the answer is written
directly under the task it answers — including when there is no answer.** The result is a document
where a reader can see not only what was concluded but where the author actually got to.

## The skeleton

Twelve of the fourteen reports in [[cybersecurity-engineering-laboratories]] share the same shape:

1. **Introduction** — the concepts the lab needs, written out before any tool is opened.
2. Numbered sections pairing prompts with answers: the cryptography labs (02–07) split each section
   into **`I. Tasks`** and **`II. Questions`**; the network and web labs (08, 10–14) fold both into a
   **`Problems and questions`** block against a task list.
3. Every answer prefixed with `>` and placed immediately under its prompt, interleaved with
   screenshots of the tool at that step.

The exceptions are informative rather than sloppy. Lab 01 is environment setup and is effectively
screenshots — roughly 400 characters of extractable text across 5 pages — and lab 12 is nearly the
same. Only lab 02 carries per-section `Conclusion` blocks; every later report drops them. The skeleton
was adopted and then simplified, not designed once and followed.

## Failure gets the same slot as success

This is what distinguishes the pattern from an ordinary answer sheet. A step that did not work is
recorded in place, at the same level of prominence as the ones that did:

> "it did not fuzz :("
> — Cybersecurity-Engineering-Laboratories/labs/13_web_security_tooling/lab-13-report.pdf, 2026-07-25

The same convention runs through the set: four consecutive OpenSSL Diffie–Hellman steps in lab 06
marked "could not extract", "not working", "did not work", "not resolved"; two lab-02 tasks marked
"Did not do."; an exploitation chain in lab 12 ending in an empty result. **None of it is deleted.**
The provenance of an answer is recorded on the same terms:

> "Thank you, the enlisted guide from university was a bit hard to grasp so i took help from a given
> video from ms teams! It was much easier to understand."
> — Cybersecurity-Engineering-Laboratories/labs/08_network_security/lab-08-report.pdf, 2026-07-25

## Why it is worth having as a pattern

Three things fall out of the shape:

- **The document is auditable against the task sheet.** Every prompt appears, so a missing answer is
  visible as a gap rather than as an absence you would have to notice.
- **A dead end is preserved.** The step that failed, and the point at which it failed, is exactly the
  information no other artefact records — the same value the wiki's own session pages place on dead
  ends.
- **The reader can locate the boundary of the author's understanding.** Which is what makes the
  reports usable evidence in this wiki: the measured work (entropy tables, timing matrices, histogram
  comparisons) is cited on the concept pages; the generic essay answers are not.

It is the report-shaped relative of [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]] — limits stated where they
occur rather than gathered into a caveats section — and of
[[document-the-failure-mode-next-to-the-fix]].

## The cost, and it is real

The polished summary written on top of these reports **overstates them**. The README frames all 182
pages as documenting "what was attempted, what the tools returned, and what the result means", which
is true of the tasks that completed and not of the many that did not. Honest raw material plus a
confident index equals [[documentation-drift]] — and it is the exact failure mode this pattern is
otherwise good at preventing. The fix is not to polish the reports; it is to let the summary inherit
their honesty.

## Scope of the claim

`confidence: high` for the recurrence — fourteen independently written deliverables read directly.
This page does **not** claim the pattern across other repositories: the neighbouring instances live on
[[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]] and [[readme-as-guided-tour]], and are a different medium
(source comments and README prose) rather than the same habit.
